source.title: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: For a summer suit that wrinkles less than pure linen, choose a linen-silk blend; the jacket and trousers also work as separates.
tips.why: Silk reduces creasing and the pieces can be reworn with jeans or a tee.

tips.text: Fresco and tropical wool suits breathe in the heat, so wool is fine in summer.
Wool-mohair is a light, crisp suiting with a slight sheen, a good alternative to tropical wool for warm-weather events.
tips.why: Mohair adds lightness and resists creasing.

tips.text: Half-lined or unlined jackets are cooler and move more easily; unlined construction needs cleaner internal seams.
tips.why: Less lining means more comfort in heat.

tips.text: Prefer canvassed jackets over fused ones; a full canvas keeps its shape for years, while fused jackets lose structure over time.
tips.why: Sewn canvas lets the cloth drape and last.

tips.text: Double-breasted jackets look right with wide peak lapels and enough structure, ideally full canvas.
tips.why: A DB needs structure to hold its shape.

tips.text: Flap pockets suit business suits, jetted pockets are more ceremonial, and patch pockets are the casual choice for blazers.
tips.why: Pocket style sets a jacket's formality.

tips.text: Choose shoulder construction to suit your posture and build: padded for structure, soft or Neapolitan for a relaxed look.
Trousers worn with a double-breasted jacket look clean with side adjusters instead of belt loops, and a single pleat adds softness.
tips.why: No belt keeps the line uninterrupted.

tips.text: For trousers meant to fall softly onto the shoe, skip the turn-up and set the final length after trying them with the shoes you'll wear.
tips.why: Hem length depends on the shoe.

tips.text: Have trousers made slightly roomy at the waist and hips; taking them in is easy, letting them out is barely possible.
tips.why: Seam allowance is usually only about a centimetre.

tips.text: Dry-clean a suit rarely, about once a season, and warn the cleaner about delicate buttons such as mother-of-pearl.
tips.why: Frequent cleaning wears out the cloth.

tips.text: A suit should feel relaxed rather than tight, with no pulling across the back or at the armholes.
tips.why: A suit that strains looks borrowed.

tips.text: A 'Made in China' label does not automatically mean poor quality; judge fabric and construction instead.
tips.why: Many factories abroad produce high-end garments.

tips.text: A summer suit in sand or brown worn with a fine short-sleeved knit or T-shirt, tonal or contrasting, makes a relaxed warm-weather look.
tips.why: Dropping the shirt and tie keeps tailoring casual in heat.

tips.text: A higher Super number means a finer, lighter, more delicate wool cloth.
tips.why: Super numbers grade how fine the wool fibre is; finer cloth feels lighter but is less hard-wearing.

outfits.outfit: jacket beige relaxed smart casual +linen +silk +suit, tshirt cream casual +silk, trousers beige relaxed smart casual +linen +suit, dress-shoes brown formal +loafers
outfits.why: A relaxed double-breasted summer suit with a silk-cotton tee: Miami Vice without the banker.

outfits.outfit: jacket beige smart casual +blazer +linen, tshirt white casual, jeans denim casual, dress-shoes brown formal +loafers
outfits.why: The suit jacket worn as a separate over jeans and a tee.
